lesson.title: Liberté & Society Sentences
lesson.subtitle: La liberté est… — build sentences converting -ité and -ance nouns into the wild.

hook.title: Abstract Ideas in Everyday Conversation
hook.content: Where English says bare 'Freedom is important' or 'Society changes', French always gives the abstract concept its definite article: La liberté est importante, La société est grande, La réalité est différente. Alongside them sits la ville ('the city', cousin of villa and village).

footnotes.title: Why French uses 'the' before abstract nouns
footnotes.content: When talking about a concept as a whole category (freedom, patience, reality, society, music), French never leaves the subject noun naked!

pattern.title: Always Keep La Before General Abstract Concepts
pattern.content: Start general statements with La liberté, La société, La réalité, La qualité + est + feminine adjective.
pattern.linguist_note: Generic definite articles are mandatory in Romance for mass and abstract nouns used as subjects.
pattern.trap_note: Never drop La at the start of 'Freedom is precious' (*Liberté est précieuse) — always say La liberté!

exercises.prompt: Match each general statement with its French rendering (keeping the article!):
exercises.target_answer: La liberté est importante, La société est grande, La ville est belle, La réalité est différente
exercises.meaning: Freedom is important, Society is big, The city is beautiful, Reality is different
exercises.explanation: French keeps La before abstract nouns when talking about them in general.

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word structure of 'La liberté est importante'?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: The liberty is important
exercises.explanation: French requires the definite article La before abstract subject nouns.
la ville is feminine, so grande takes -e.

cues: is very different → est très différente
idea_parts: verb + adverb + adj → est très différente
exercises.target_answer: La réalité est très différente ici
exercises.explanation: La réalité requires the article La and feminine différente.

diagnosis.cue: Start with La réalité and end différente with -e.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: La société et la ville sont grandes
exercises.target_answer: La société et la ville sont grandes
exercises.meaning: The society and the city are big
exercises.explanation: Two feminine nouns joined by et take plural sont grandes.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote sont grandes with the feminine plural -es.

summary.outcome: Construct general statements about society, freedom, quality, and the city using mandatory definite articles.

use_example.german: La qualité est très importante dans cette ville.
use_example.english: Quality is very important in this city.

summary.takeaway: Never leave an abstract noun bare in French: 'Freedom' is always La liberté.

liberté.etymology_derivation: liberté/liberty — the Norman doublet in -ité form: same Latin liber, two carriers.

ville.etymology_derivation: Latin vīlla 'country estate' grew into the whole city in French (leaving 'city' as la cité for the historic core).

différence.etymology_derivation: Latin differentia. The -ance/-ence endings convert whole and are always feminine.

être.etymology_derivation: Latin esse 'to be' → essere → être. English kept the root in essence and quintessential — the being-ness inside the word.

très.etymology_derivation: Latin trāns 'across' — très means 'beyond, across the line'. English kept the same root in transmit and transatlantic.

ite.name: The -ité Bridge
ite.phonetic_rule: English final -ity becomes stressed final -ité /ite/ — the é marks the syllable English swallows.
ite.historical_linguistics: Latin -itās survives in English -ity and French -ité; both are bookish layers grafted onto the everyday vocabulary, which is why they convert with no sound loss.
ite.philological_note: All -ité nouns are feminine (la possibilité, la liberté).
ite.literature_source: Pope (1952); Brunot, Histoire de la langue française.
